style: An antique brain-atlas: the cortex drawn as a hand-mapped terrain of ridges and shaded regions, with waves of ink-wash shading sweeping over it like tides on an old chart — a register suited to an article that keeps describing the brain's surface in terms of stencils, fields, and traveling patterns.

plates.title: From Fixed Neurons to Conscious Waves
plates.prompt: An antique brain-atlas page, cortex drawn as a hand-mapped terrain with ridges and shaded regions, ink-wash and sepia palette on aged paper, reading top to bottom as a single descending path. At the top: MILLIONS COORDINATED IN AN INSTANT, a packed crowd of tiny figures under one commanding hand. Below, enter the labeled area 'MULTIFUNCTIONAL NEURONS NEED A ROUTER': ONE NEURON, ONE FIXED JOB with a cartouche of FIGURE A (feedforward hierarchy rising to a cat/dog), then SAME CELL, TWO ANSWERS (one cell lit two ways), then SYNCHRONY WITHOUT WIRES (cells glowing together with no wire-threads). The path narrows into the second labeled area 'SPATIAL COMPUTING & TRAVELING WAVES': THE STENCIL LAID OVER CORTEX with a cartouche of FIGURE C's colored regions, INSIDE OR OUTSIDE THE SHADOW, THE WAVE DRAGS THE STATE ACROSS, and TWO WAVES MEETING MAKE A THIRD with a small FIGURE F inset of crossing sine-waves. Continuing down, outside both labeled areas: THREE DRUGS, ONE FLAT WAVE (three vials pouring into one slow wave), THE CLOSED LOOP OF THE THREE (circular synapse-spike-wave chain with a FIGURE H cartouche), and off to one side in a small medallion, set apart from the main vertical path: FIELDS, NOT A TOWN CRIER. At the very bottom, the full terrain: THE WHOLE TERRAIN UNDER ONE WAVE, cortex entirely joined under a single sweep of shading. Draw the two labeled areas as enclosed regions on the map (bordered with a faint double line) so they read as distinct zones from the unenclosed steps before and after them. No lettering anywhere except the twelve titles exactly as given, lettered beneath each vignette in a plain antique hand; no other words, banners, or inscriptions anywhere on the page.

vignettes.quote: a given neuron's spikes always "mean" the same unique thing
vignettes.depicts: A row of labeled cells each wearing a fixed badge (a single mark that never changes), drawn as an old guild chart of specialists, beside a small inset cartouche of FIGURE A showing the feedforward hierarchy of lines and edges rising to a cat and dog.
vignettes.title: ONE NEURON, ONE FIXED JOB

vignettes.quote: A neuron might spike to object A, but only when it was seen first
vignettes.depicts: A single cell drawn twice side by side, lit only in the left scene (object seen first) and dark in the right (same object seen second), showing one cell answering differently depending on order.
vignettes.title: SAME CELL, TWO ANSWERS

vignettes.quote: temporary inhibitory "stencils" across the surface of cortex
vignettes.depicts: A hand reaching down to lay a perforated stencil-plate over the cortical terrain, shadow falling through its cut-out holes onto patches of ground below, with FIGURE C's blue and purple regions rendered as the stencil's painted zones.
vignettes.title: THE STENCIL LAID OVER CORTEX

vignettes.quote: may lie inside the inhibitory stencil in one context and outside it in another
vignettes.depicts: The same cell drawn at two positions relative to the stencil's shadow-line, lit when outside it and dimmed when inside, with small arrows showing context swapping its position.
vignettes.title: INSIDE OR OUTSIDE THE SHADOW

vignettes.quote: alpha/beta waves may constitute a control mechanism that transitions cortical population activity from one subspace to another
vignettes.depicts: A wave-crest shown mid-sweep across the terrain, with a trail of footprints bending from one marked region of ground to a second, distinct region, as though pulled along by the wave's passage.
vignettes.title: THE WAVE DRAGS THE STATE ACROSS

vignettes.quote: they naturally add together, cancel out, or form new patterns through their superposition and interference
vignettes.depicts: Two ink-wash wave patterns crossing on the terrain, their overlap darkened where they add and left pale where they cancel, forming a new woven pattern at the crossing, with FIGURE F's two sine-waves rendered as a small cartouche beside it.
vignettes.title: TWO WAVES MEETING MAKE A THIRD

vignettes.quote: propofol (GABAergic), ketamine (NMDAergic), and dexmedetomidine (alpha-2 adrenergic), all converge on similar large-scale electrical effects
vignettes.depicts: Three separate small vials or flasks, each marked with its own distinct emblem, pouring into the same single slow, flattened wave-pattern drawn across the cortical terrain.
vignettes.title: THREE DRUGS, ONE FLAT WAVE

vignettes.quote: Synapses shape spiking, spiking contributes to brain waves, and waves shape spiking
vignettes.depicts: A closed circular chain drawn over the terrain: a root-like synapse network feeding up into a spike, the spike radiating into a wave-ring, and the wave-ring curving back down into the roots, with FIGURE H's hybrid diagram as a framed inset.
vignettes.title: THE CLOSED LOOP OF THE THREE

vignettes.quote: emphasize how this integration occurs via dynamic field interactions rather than broadcasting of information
vignettes.depicts: Set apart in a side medallion off the main path: a wave-pattern linking scattered regions of the terrain directly, contrasted with a faint ghost-image of a town-crier broadcasting from a tower, crossed out lightly.
vignettes.title: FIELDS, NOT A TOWN CRIER

vignettes.quote: Consciousness, then, emerges when these dynamic wave patterns bring the cortex into an organized, globally integrated state
vignettes.depicts: At the foot of the map, the whole cortical terrain shown at last bathed in one single continuous wave-pattern, all its separate shaded regions now joined under one unbroken sweep of shading.
vignettes.title: THE WHOLE TERRAIN UNDER ONE WAVE

plates.title: Why Mixed Selectivity Needs a Router
plates.prompt: An antique brain-atlas plate, same sepia ink-wash register as the overview, opening with the stencil-and-grid image this plate zooms into from the top. Down the page in order: A THIRD OF ALL CELLS AT ONCE, a torn-open stencil revealing a grid of cells with one in three lit. THREADS BRAIDED INTO ONE CELL, a cell with several different threads woven into it. LIGHT THAT SHIFTS WITH CONTEXT, two small paired panels of one cell lit differently under a shifting banner, drawn as a cartouche beside FIGURE B's pure-vs-mixed task diagram. MANY BASKETS, MIXED GOODS, a storehouse of overlapping baskets beside crossed-out single-good storerooms. ONE CELL, MANY CIRCLES, a figure stepping between overlapping drawn circles. A TANGLE WITH NO KEY, a dense criss-crossed web with a confused figure holding an unused key. THE WAVE SORTS THE TANGLE, a wave-ring over the same tangle, now sorting it into bundles. SYNCHRONY WITH THE WIRES CUT, a ring of glowing cells with their connecting wires visibly severed. THE RIPPLE OUTRUNS THE SIGNAL, a wave spreading instantly across the terrain beside a slow crawling spike-signal on a single thread. At the bottom, THE HAND THAT ROUTES THE TANGLE, a hand brightening one cluster and dimming another. Compose as a single descending column using the full width of the page, each vignette large enough to read clearly, spaced with bare paper rather than crowding; one cartouche inset of FIGURE B placed beside its matching vignette. No lettering anywhere on the page except the ten titles exactly as given, in a plain antique hand beneath each scene.

vignettes.quote: any given task engages around a third of all neurons in the prefrontal cortex
vignettes.depicts: Opening the same stencil image from the overview, now torn open to reveal underneath it a packed grid of cells where one in every three is marked lit for a single task.
vignettes.title: A THIRD OF ALL CELLS AT ONCE

vignettes.quote: neurons reflect nonlinear combinations of variables, often integrating
vignettes.depicts: A single cell drawn with several threads of different kinds braided into it at once — one marked for object, one for order, one for action — tangled together rather than separate.
vignettes.title: THREADS BRAIDED INTO ONE CELL

vignettes.quote: selective spiking to objects that changes depending on the context of their sequence order
vignettes.depicts: Two small paired scenes of the same cell lit differently under a shifting context-banner above it, showing its light changing as the banner changes.
vignettes.title: LIGHT THAT SHIFTS WITH CONTEXT

vignettes.quote: information is multiplexed across many multifunctional neurons rather than segregated into specialist neurons
vignettes.depicts: A storehouse drawn with many small overlapping baskets each holding a mix of goods, contrasted with a faint crossed-out row of single-good storerooms beside it.
vignettes.title: MANY BASKETS, MIXED GOODS

vignettes.quote: cortical neurons have the capacity to participate in multiple networks, shifting membership as needed
vignettes.depicts: A single figure standing at the overlap of several drawn circles (networks), stepping from one circle's edge into another's as dotted footprints trace its shifting membership.
vignettes.title: ONE CELL, MANY CIRCLES

vignettes.quote: dynamically routing signals through a dense web of overlapping networks
vignettes.depicts: A dense tangle of criss-crossing threads across the terrain with a small confused figure standing before it holding an unused key, unable to find which thread to pull.
vignettes.title: A TANGLE WITH NO KEY

vignettes.quote: organizing information, routing it between circuits, and coordinating memory and control processes
vignettes.depicts: A wave-ring appearing over the tangle from the previous scene, visibly sorting the threads beneath it into three separated bundles labeled by their separate paths.
vignettes.title: THE WAVE SORTS THE TANGLE

vignettes.quote: spread through the local tissue at the speed of electromagnetic propagation, making them effectively instantaneous
vignettes.depicts: A wave-ripple shown spreading outward across the whole terrain in one single frozen instant, while beside it a lone spike-signal is still shown crawling slowly along a single long thread.
vignettes.title: THE RIPPLE OUTRUNS THE SIGNAL

vignettes.quote: activate or suppress ensembles, and flexibly route information across overlapping networks
vignettes.depicts: At the foot of the scene, a single hand (the wave) reaching down to brighten one cluster of cells and dim another, the same tangle from before now calmly routed.
vignettes.title: THE HAND THAT ROUTES THE TANGLE

plates.title: Stencils, Traveling Waves, and Wave Arithmetic
plates.prompt: An antique brain-atlas plate in the same sepia ink-wash register, opening with the stencil-image this plate zooms into, carried over from the overview. Down the page: BETA AS A BRAKE ON THE ROAD, a brake-lever on a cortical road pressed down then released beside a running figure. THE STENCIL RETURNS, the perforated stencil laid over the terrain with light through its holes. CONFIRMED IN THE MONKEY'S CORTEX, a scholar's lens over a small monkey figure checking the stencil's shadow against the ground. THE MIDDLE SCALE FITS BEST, a measuring-compass comparing three scales against the stencil's own holes. CAUGHT UNDER THE SHADOW OR NOT, one cell drawn twice, shadowed and clear, beside a cartouche of FIGURE D's grid. A FLOCK MOVING AS ONE BAND, a flock of birds banking together over the terrain. THE WAVE'S TRAILING FURROW, a wave-crest sweeping across leaving a visible furrow, beside a cartouche of FIGURE E's shifting stencil. THE FLOCK BENT ONTO A NEW PATH, the same flock bent by the wave onto a new banked route. ADDING AND CANCELING WAVES, two wave-patterns crossing, darkened and pale where they add and cancel, beside a cartouche of FIGURE F's two sine-waves. At the bottom, SETTLING AT ONCE, NOT STEP BY STEP, the whole terrain resolved into one calm wave-pattern beside a faint ghost-figure climbing a stepwise staircase. Arrange as a single wide descending column filling the page's width and height, each vignette large and uncrowded, three cartouche insets (FIGURE D, FIGURE E, FIGURE F) placed beside their matching scenes, drawn in the manuscript's own hand rather than pasted flat. No lettering anywhere on the page except the ten titles exactly as given, lettered beneath each scene in a plain antique hand; no other words.

vignettes.quote: beta acts like a brake on movement execution
vignettes.depicts: Opening the plate: a cortical road drawn with a literal brake-lever set into the ground, pressed down hard in one scene and released in a neighboring one, where a small running figure then moves freely.
vignettes.title: BETA AS A BRAKE ON THE ROAD

vignettes.quote: temporary inhibitory "stencils" across the surface of cortex
vignettes.depicts: The stencil-plate from the overview laid down again over the terrain, its cut-out holes letting light fall through onto open patches of ground.
vignettes.title: THE STENCIL RETURNS

vignettes.quote: examining prefrontal cortex activity in non-human primates during complex cognitive tasks
vignettes.depicts: A scholar's hand holding a magnifying lens over a small figure of a monkey seated before the cortical terrain, confirming the stencil's shadow-pattern matches the ground beneath.
vignettes.title: CONFIRMED IN THE MONKEY'S CORTEX

vignettes.quote: extend over a range of a few millimeters, might be just the right spatial scale for top-down control
vignettes.depicts: A measuring-compass set against the terrain comparing three marked scales — a tiny one, a vast one, and a middle one fitted exactly to the stencil's own holes.
vignettes.title: THE MIDDLE SCALE FITS BEST

vignettes.quote: may lie inside the inhibitory stencil in one context and outside it in another
vignettes.depicts: The same cell drawn twice, once caught under the stencil's shadow and once standing clear of it, paired with a cartouche of FIGURE D's grid of two objects by two contexts.
vignettes.title: CAUGHT UNDER THE SHADOW OR NOT

vignettes.quote: population spiking tends to occupy a lower-dimensional "subspace" or "manifold"
vignettes.depicts: A great flock of small birds all moving together across the terrain in a single narrow banked formation rather than scattering independently.
vignettes.title: A FLOCK MOVING AS ONE BAND

vignettes.quote: sweep across the cortical surface, tracing complex, but highly organized, spatiotemporal patterns
vignettes.depicts: A long wave-crest shown mid-journey sweeping across the terrain leaving a visible trailing furrow behind it, paired with a cartouche of FIGURE E's shifting stencil-to-stencil transition.
vignettes.title: THE WAVE'S TRAILING FURROW

vignettes.quote: transitions cortical population activity from one subspace to another
vignettes.depicts: The flock of birds from before shown mid-turn, bent by the passing wave-crest from one banked path onto a second, different banked path.
vignettes.title: THE FLOCK BENT ONTO A NEW PATH

vignettes.quote: they naturally add together, cancel out, or form new patterns through their superposition and interference
vignettes.depicts: Two separate wave-patterns crossing over the terrain, darkened where they add and pale where they cancel, forming a new woven third pattern, with a cartouche of FIGURE F's two sine-waves.
vignettes.title: ADDING AND CANCELING WAVES

vignettes.quote: does not loop through variables but settles into a solution as a whole
vignettes.depicts: At the foot of the plate, the whole terrain settling at once into a single calm resolved wave-pattern, contrasted with a faint ghost-figure walking a long stepwise staircase beside it, one step at a time.
vignettes.title: SETTLING AT ONCE, NOT STEP BY STEP
